twin_rejecting.evidence: electrical.power.motor_current_draw and motor_power_draw (design/nodes/electrical.power.json, rev 31) were rewritten by this revision (new source citations [R1a.04] in place of [R1.03]) and still equal the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current (1.5 A) used directly against the node's own declared 7.2 V supply_voltage, without the V_max scaling (I_stall,max = V_max/R) the electrical standards (§5) and skill file require; the standards file's own worked example for this identical 1.5 A/6 V motor shows the scaled value (~2.1 A at 8.4 V) exceeds the DRV8838's 1.8 A peak rating and 1.9 A minimum trip, a comparison never made anywhere in the graph. The revision is therefore not consistent with the electrical standards it is held to.

electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw (rewritten, rev 31) are never compared against any continuous or peak/current-limit rating of a supply element; the DRV8838 datasheet is already cited elsewhere in the same node for thermal_resistance, so its ratings are derivable and this comparison was the revision's duty.

No determination of the lowest rating in the motor branch's series path appears anywhere in the graph; the driver's own peak/continuous current rating is derivable from its already-cited datasheet and was not sourced or compared when the motor-branch load was rewritten.

electrical.power.motor_current_draw, a load drawn from electrical.battery_pack, was rewritten, but no node compares total pack current against the NiMH maker's 4C discharge-rate limit; the cell type/part is given (untouched), so this is not a missing input.
Every battery-rail check in the graph uses only the single nominal value 7.2 V; no check exists at the top of the window or the sagged bottom, for the rewritten motor-branch load.

electrical.power.motor_current_draw (rev 31) = [R1a.04] * [R1.25] = 1.5 A (stall current at the motor's 6 V rated voltage) x 2, used directly at the node's own declared 7.2 V supply_voltage, with no I_stall,max = V_max/R scaling; standards §5's own worked example for this identical 1.5 A/6 V rating gives about 2.1 A at the pack's 8.4 V top.

No node records the DRV8838's continuous rating, peak rating or minimum OCP trip, and no comparison against the stall current appears anywhere; standards §5 shows the scaled current (~2.1 A at 8.4 V) exceeds the 1.8 A peak rating and the 1.9 A minimum trip.
No node states how long a stall may last or what ends it for the new motor, and no continuous-current-vs-stall-current guidance is recorded anywhere.
No derating table exists for the motor or driver branch anywhere in the graph, despite this revision changing a power-path part (the motor).
All battery-rail quantities touched by this revision use only the single nominal 7.2 V value; no top-of-window or sagged-bottom check exists.

electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw use the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current compared/used at the pack's higher nominal 7.2 V (and higher still at 8.4 V) without scaling, the exact antipattern named.

electrical.motors.stall_current (rewritten) and electrical.motor_drivers' ratings are each recorded alone; the required combination (stall current scaled to V_max, compared with the driver's peak rating and minimum OCP trip) is never performed, and by reading (R=6V/1.5A=4 ohm; I at 8.4V=2.1A) it fails against the DRV8838's 1.8 A peak rating and 1.9 A minimum trip cited in this project's own standards file.

The revision is not internally consistent: mechanical.gearboxes.no_load_speed ('derived: [R1a.10]/[R2.12]' = 45.0 rad/s / 218.5 = 0.206 rad/s) and reaction_moment/torque_peak ('derived: [R1a.13]*[R2.12]' = 1.1 kgf*cm * 218.5 = 240 kgf*cm), plus the matching control.balance_loop.torque_peak and control.speed_loop.no_load_speed, divide/multiply the gearmotor's already internally-geared output figures (R1a.10, R1a.13, both past the motor's own 75.81:1 internal reduction) by the overall ratio R2.12=218.5 (which already contains that same internal 75.81:1 reduction), double-counting it. Correct values using the node's own external_gear_ratio=2.88 would be about 15.6 rad/s (149 rpm) and 3.17 kgf*cm, not 0.206 rad/s and 240 kgf*cm (23.5 N*m from a 9.5 g motor pair, implausible on its face). Separately, electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified ('the drivers see the same 7.2 V supply and the new motor's 1.5 A stall current equals the old one, so the driver load is unchanged') substitutes a nominal-voltage comparison for the required pack-top-voltage (V_max, ~8.4 V) stall-current bound (ES-14/ES-15/ES-16), and electrical.motors carries no manufacturer part number for the new #3074 part (model: null) despite the part being replaced (ES-5).

electrical.motors.json (rev 30) replaces the motor from #3073 to #3074 but its top-level 'model' field remains null (as it was before), and no quantity in the node records a manufacturer part number for #3074; the cited sources are bare product/specs URLs with no explicit datasheet revision beyond the one PDF ('pololu-micro-metal-gearmotors-rev-6-2.pdf') used only for rated_voltage/supply_voltage, not for the other ratings used (current_draw, gear_ratio, stall_torque, no_load_speed, etc.).

electrical.power (rev 31) records motor_current_draw=3.0 A and motor_power_draw=21.6 W but no node in the graph (electrical.power, electrical.motor_drivers, or the unchanged electrical.battery_pack) records a comparison of this draw against any continuous or peak/current-limit rating; no margin or closure figure is declared anywhere, even though this quantity is a written value in this change set.

electrical.power.motor_current_draw (a load drawn from the battery) was rewritten for the new motor, but electrical.battery_pack (unchanged) carries no discharge-rate quantity, and no node compares the 3.0 A combined stall draw against the NiMH maker's sourced maximum discharge rate (4C, per the Energizer NiMH handbook already cited in the electrical standards file); the cell type/chemistry is not named as an explicit quantity on electrical.battery_pack either.

No quantity anywhere checks the new motor or the unchanged driver at the top of the battery's voltage window (V_max, about 8.4 V for 6 NiMH cells per the electrical standards file's own derivation); electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified uses only the nominal 7.2 V supply_voltage.

electrical.motors.stall_current (1.5 A, rewritten and sourced to the #3074 specs page) is used as-is at the 6 V rated voltage; no node computes I_stall,max = V_max/R (R = 6 V / 1.5 A = 4 ohm) at the pack's highest voltage (~8.4 V, giving ~2.1 A per the electrical standards file's own worked example for this motor family). electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified instead compares only at the nominal 7.2 V supply.

No node declares the DRV8838's continuous rating, peak rating (1.8 A) or minimum OCP trip (1.9 A, both cited in the already-referenced TI SLVSBA4F datasheet used for thermal_resistance on this same node) nor compares the new motor's V_max-scaled stall current against them; electrical.motor_drivers (rev 32) adds only a nominal-voltage equivalence justification.

No node states how long a stall may last for the new motor or what ends it, and no continuous-current-vs-25%-of-stall-current check is recorded for #3074; this was not addressed when the motor was swapped.

electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified compares the new and old motor only 'at the same 7.2 V supply' (nominal), never at the pack's top (~8.4 V) or sagged-bottom voltage, matching this antipattern directly.

The stall-current comparison implicit in electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified uses the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current (1.5 A) rather than the value scaled to the pack's highest voltage, while the pack's highest voltage (~8.4 V) is higher than 6 V - exactly the antipattern this item names.

electrical.motor_drivers' no_change_justified computes equivalence only at the nominal 7.2 V supply using the unchanged rated-voltage (6 V) stall current (a value the revision wrote for #3074), while the electrical standards file explicitly requires the stall-current check to be redone at the pack's highest voltage (~8.4 V, SS4-SS5), where the bound (~2.1 A) would exceed the DRV8838's cited peak (1.8 A) and trip (1.9 A) ratings; the harder, standards-required condition is never evaluated.

The revision's own cited formula for counts_per_wheel_revolution ('derived: [R3.02] * [R2.14]' = 12 × 127.3 = 1527.6) does not hold the written value 1530 in design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json and design/nodes/firmware.odometry.json (journal.jsonl rev 35 and rev 37); and the gear-ratio change (which lowered torque_peak from 110 to 94.2 kgf*cm) triggers MS-28 but no wheel-torque/traction/current margin or governing-limit statement was added anywhere in the design graph. The revision is therefore not fully consistent with the design it changes.

design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json and design/nodes/firmware.odometry.json write counts_per_wheel_revolution = 1530 with source 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.14]'. R3.02 = 12 (parts_sheet.json) and R2.14 = 127.3 (parts_sheet.json), so the cited source computes 12 × 127.3 = 1527.6, not 1530. The source does not hold the value.

counts_per_wheel_revolution = 1530 in control.speed_loop.json and firmware.odometry.json does not match its cited source arithmetic (12×127.3 = 1527.6); all other changed magnitudes (gear_ratio 127.3, external_gear_ratio 2.47, no_load_speed 0.535 rad/s, torque_peak/reaction_moment 94.2 kgf*cm) check out against their sources and neighbouring values.

The revision resizes the gear ratio (mechanical.gearboxes.json gear_ratio 148.3→127.3, external_gear_ratio 2.88→2.47), lowering torque_peak from 110 to 94.2 kgf*cm, which triggers this item. No node touched by the revision, nor any other node in the graph (electrical.motors.json, mechanical.wheel_left.json, mechanical.wheel_right.json were read and contain no such check), states a wheel-torque-vs-usable-gearmotor-torque×ratio comparison, a motor-current-vs-25%-stall check, a stated operating margin, or which limit governs. These are derivable from parts_sheet.json (R1.07 stall torque, R1.03 stall current) and the revision's own written ratio, so they are the revision's duty, not a missing input.

counts_per_wheel_revolution = 1530 in design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json and design/nodes/firmware.odometry.json (journal.jsonl rev 35, rev 37), citing source 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.14]' = 12 × 127.3 = 1527.6, not 1530; the written number differs from what the revision's own cited calculation returns, and it replaced a different prior value (1780), so it is the revision's own chosen number.

The revision rewrote mechanical.gearboxes' gear_ratio (110.2) and external_gear_ratio (2.14) in design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json (journal.jsonl rev 30) without ever stating, anywhere in the design graph, a drive-torque/traction margin or which limit governs for the new ratio, as MS-28 requires whenever a gear ratio is resized. The revision is therefore not consistent with the mechanical standards/rubric it must satisfy.

mechanical.gearboxes.json (rev 30) resizes gear_ratio (148.3→110.2) and external_gear_ratio (2.88→2.14). MS-28 requires that whenever a gear ratio is sized, the design states which limit governs (traction vs. motor) and a torque/traction margin with its reason. No node in the design graph (mechanical.*, control.*, firmware.*, electrical.*) states such a margin, a governing limit, or a motor-current check against the 25% stall-current rule for the new 110.2 ratio. Every input such a check needs — stall torque R1.07=0.74 kgf*cm, wheel diameter R9.01=80 mm, robot mass 330 g, and typical μ_s values from the skill table — is already present or derivable from parts_sheet.json and the design graph, so this is the revision's own unmet duty, not a missing input.

control.speed_loop.counts_per_wheel_revolution and firmware.odometry.counts_per_wheel_revolution are both written to 1150 with source 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.20]', but 12 * 96.2 = 1154.4, not 1150 (parts_sheet.json R3.02=12, R2.20=96.2). The superseded value (1780) matched its own formula (12*148.3=1779.6). In addition, the gear-ratio change (mechanical.gearboxes/mechanical.drivetrain) triggers MS-28 (drive sizing) and no usable-torque-vs-demand check, governing-limit statement, or margin was written anywhere in the touched nodes. The revision is therefore not fully consistent with the design it changes or with this rubric.

control.speed_loop.json and firmware.odometry.json (journal.jsonl rev 35, rev 37) record counts_per_wheel_revolution=1150 sourced to 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.20]'; parts_sheet.json gives R3.02=12 (encoder disc resolution) and R2.20=96.2 (overall gear ratio), whose product is 1154.4. The cited source does not hold the recorded value.

counts_per_wheel_revolution (control.speed_loop.json, firmware.odometry.json) is recorded as 1150 where its own cited neighbours (R3.02=12, R2.20=96.2) and formula give 1154.4 -- a magnitude that does not match its source or the values it depends on, despite every other magnitude in the same revision (external_gear_ratio 1.87, gear_ratio 96.2, no_load_speed 0.708 rad/s, torque_peak/reaction_moment 71.2 kgf*cm) checking out exactly against parts_sheet.json.

mechanical.gearboxes.gear_ratio and external_gear_ratio are written (148.3->96.2, 2.88->1.87), which is a drive-sizing change, but no node written by this revision states a usable-torque-vs-demand comparison, says which limit (motor torque vs traction) governs, or gives a margin with its reason, as MS-28 requires. The traction/mu_s sub-check (tractive force <= mu_s*N; mu_s for the stated floor) cannot be judged at all because no floor-surface or mu_s quantity exists anywhere in the design graph (see blocking spec defect below); the usable-torque-budget and governing-limit/margin sub-checks, however, are decidable from quantities already in the graph (stall torque, gear ratio, robot mass) and are simply missing, so the item is a finding independent of the blocked sub-check.

control.speed_loop.json and firmware.odometry.json both record counts_per_wheel_revolution=1150 under 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.20]', a value the revision wrote (changed from 1780), but 12 * 96.2 = 1154.4, not 1150: the written value differs from what its own cited formula computes.

design/nodes/mechanical.bumper_cage.json (journal rev 30) is newly written by the revision with only a mass quantity; per std §15/MS-30 every added part needs a stated clearance to the ground and neighbouring parts in the balancing pose, and parts_sheet.json's own ground-clearance row R10.06 is null, so no such value exists anywhere the revision could have read it. The revision itself introduces this unchecked interface (also MH-1), making it inconsistent with the rubric's MS-30 requirement; this is a condition the revision wrote, not a given-value condition, so it is not excused by the clause-B 'Given values' rule.

design/nodes/mechanical.bumper_cage.json (journal rev 30) adds a new physical part with only a mass quantity; no clearance value to the ground or to any neighbouring part in the balancing pose is stated for it anywhere in the design graph, and parts_sheet.json's own 'ground clearance (80 mm wheels)' row R10.06 is recorded null (no value captured from its source), so the value cannot be read from the given data either. std §15/MS-30 requires every added part's clearance to the ground and to moving/fixed neighbours in the balancing pose to be stated with a tolerance basis; none is given.

mechanical.bumper_cage (design/nodes/mechanical.bumper_cage.json, rev 30) is added with only a mass quantity; the design graph contains no calculation or stated value checking its clearance to the ground, to the wheels, or its mounting interface to mechanical.robot in the assembled/balancing pose. The interface never checked is the bumper cage's clearance to the ground that std §1/§15 call out as a known concern for this platform.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30 raises control.balance_loop.loop_gain 2.5→3.0 with source text 'design: proportional gain ... raised for a stiffer tilt response' and no accompanying plant model, validity region, pole/margin computation, crossover or delay statement, or simulation anywhere in the design graph (control.balance_loop.json, firmware.balance_task.json, firmware.main.json, and every other node). Because the revision wrote the exact gain that governs the unstable loop's stability, these omissions are the revision's own duties (rule 7's 'a duty of the work is never a missing input', explicitly illustrated by D30's bandwidth example), not missing inputs. A gain increase on an unstable plant asserted only by prose, with zero verification, is inconsistent with the rubric's domain standards (D1, D3, D6-D9, D17, D23, D29, D30, D33).

No node in the design graph (before or after the revision) states a tilt-angle, speed or load validity region for any linear/linearised model of control.balance_loop; the revision's rewritten node (control.balance_loop.json) carries only loop_gain, mass, sample_rate, torque_peak, no validity-region field. Since the revision wrote the gain this check is about, the absence is the revision's duty, not a missing input.

The revision's own performance claim ('raised for a stiffer tilt response', journal rev 30) is made with no stated operating region at all (see D1), so it cannot be shown to stay inside any declared region.
No quantity anywhere in the design graph records closed-loop pole locations or eigenvalues for the revised loop (loop_gain=3.0); no computation of this kind exists in any node.
No stated encirclement count or unstable-pole count P, and no pole computation (D3), exists anywhere in the design graph for the revised loop.
No evidence of a pole/zero cancellation check (full closed-loop poles, S/PS/CS/T stability, or a PID-root check) exists anywhere for the revised gain.

The cat.-2 stating line (ω_gc, n_gc, τ_total, τ_common, any common RHP zero) is owed regardless of [B] and is never stated anywhere in the design graph for either the 2.5 or the 3.0 gain; since the revision wrote the gain this stating line concerns, its absence is the revision's own failure.
The cat.-2 RHP-zero stating line (owed regardless of [B]) is never made for any fed-back signal of the revised loop; no 'none found' statement or zero list appears anywhere in the design graph.

The cat.-2 stating line requiring motor/driver and IMU/filter bandwidths 'with sources' (an explicit duty-of-the-work example in the rubric's own policy rule 7 text) is never provided; electrical.motors.json and electrical.imu.json carry voltage/current/speed/torque specs but no bandwidth figure anywhere.
No gain or phase margin quantity is recorded for control.balance_loop (or any node) at gain=2.5 or gain=3.0; no computation is shown anywhere in the design graph.

No design case (LQR guarantee, discrete LQR, or 'any other design') is stated anywhere, and no margins exist to check against a floor; control.balance_loop.json records only loop_gain/mass/sample_rate/torque_peak.

Trigger present: control.tilt_estimator ('gyro and accelerometer fusion', a complementary-filter estimator) sits in the fed-back path to control.balance_loop. No margin computation exists on any loop, so none can be shown to include this filter.
No lower gain margin (GML) or stability margin s_m is reported anywhere for the revised loop.
No M_s or M_T sensitivity-peak values are reported anywhere for the revised loop.
No gain margin value of any kind is recorded anywhere (see D7/D10), so there is no unit label to check for ratio/dB confusion; this sub-check has nothing to evaluate absent an underlying margin.

No crossover frequency ω_c or ratio h·ω_c is ever argued; control.req_sample_rate.json and control.balance_loop.json state sample_rate=100 Hz only as 'minimum update rate for the balance loop' with no ratio to any computed closed-loop frequency, before or after the gain change that would shift ω_c.
No continuous-time margin computation or hold/filter phase-cost term (0.5·ω_c·h) appears anywhere to check against a budget, consistent with the total absence of any margin computation (D7).

The cat.-2 stating line (τ_total, τ_common, owed regardless of [B]) and the τ_unmodelled < PM/ω_gc check (also owed regardless of [B]) are never stated or computed anywhere in the design graph, although the revision wrote the gain that sets the loop's margin budget.
No statement of A/D resolution or coefficient word length (the cat.-2 stating line) appears anywhere in the design graph for the revised gain, nor any numerical-sensitivity simulation.

Magnitude limit is declared as a given value (firmware.motor_output.json: motor_voltage_limit=6V, max_duty_cycle=0.833, untouched by this revision) — met for that part. A rate limit is absent from the entire design graph and cannot be derived from the given motor data (no inductance/electrical time-constant figures exist anywhere to compute a slew-rate limit); since this node was not written by the revision, this is a genuine missing input under rule 10's Given values, and the sub-check is marked [B: no rate limit].

Trigger present (control.tilt_estimator is an observer/estimator in the loop). 'Confirm the observer is fed the saturated (actuator-model) input' requires reading controller implementation code, which does not exist anywhere in this design-graph-only revision (no source files are listed in files-01-of-01.md); this input is absent from the design graph altogether and not derivable from it, with no [B] marker on this specific sub-check.
No step response, disturbance rejection, or saturating run is recorded anywhere in the design graph for either gain value; this duty is owed regardless of [B].

No run from the edge of any declared operating range, under actuator limits, is recorded anywhere; this duty is owed regardless of [B], yet the revision raised the stabilizing gain with zero recovery verification.

No simulation record of any kind exists in the design graph (see D23/D33), so there is nothing to compare for consistency with the delivered gains/sample period/estimator/limits; no [B] marker applies.
No simulation run exists at any operating point, nominal or edge (see D23/D33), and no margin/pole computation exists at any edge point either, so the override does not apply.

No control simulation of any kind exists in the design graph, so none incorporates the declared actuator limit (motor_voltage_limit=6V, max_duty_cycle=0.833 in firmware.motor_output.json); the gain was raised with no check that the stiffer response does not drive the actuator into saturation.

sample_rate=100 Hz is carried unchanged with source text 'design: inner tilt loop rate, meets control.req_sample_rate' / 'minimum update rate for the balance loop' — no ratio to any computed closed-loop frequency is argued, even after the gain change that would shift that frequency, matching the skill file's named antipattern of a round-number default with no stated ratio.
No composed run of controller+estimator+saturation+discretisation exists anywhere in the design graph for either gain value; no simulation record of any kind is present (see D23/D24/D33).

control.balance_loop.json's loop_gain is a literal (3.0) with source 'design: proportional gain ... raised for a stiffer tilt response' and no producing computation, script, or tuning procedure shown anywhere in the design graph or journal.

The journal (rev 30) claims the gain was 'raised for a stiffer tilt response', a stability/performance claim, while no observation anywhere in the design graph (no margin, pole, or simulated response) shows the loop is in fact stiffer or still stable at gain=3.0.

No node in the design graph (mechanical.*, electrical.*, control.*) records a tilt-angle, speed or load validity range for the linearised balance model; not derivable from the recorded mass/torque/voltage figures.
Cannot be judged without D1's region, which is undefined in the design graph.

No closed-loop pole computation appears in any node; forming the state matrix needs the plant's unstable pole p, which is not derivable (no inertia or CoM height is recorded anywhere, e.g. mechanical.robot.json only gives mass and overall_height).
No Nyquist/open-loop pole count or imaginary-axis handling is stated anywhere; same missing plant-model input as D3.
No pole/zero data exists for either loop; cannot check cancellation against a p that is not derivable.

The [B: p] bound cannot be evaluated (p missing, as D3). Its Cat.2 stating lines (omega_gc, n_gc, tau_total, tau_common, z) are also absent, but only for control.balance_loop/firmware.balance_task, which this revision did not write (control.balance_loop.json rev 20, unchanged) - a given-value gap, not the revision's duty.

The [B: p] sub-checks (z/p<6 override, and the p>z stable-controller-impossible check) cannot be evaluated since p is not derivable (as D3). The Cat.2 stating line (listing RHP zeros of the fed-back signals) is also absent, a given-value gap on the untouched balance/speed plant model.

The [B: p] bandwidth sub-check (10*p) cannot be evaluated (p missing). The Cat.2 stating lines (motor/driver and IMU/filter bandwidths, with sources) are also absent from the graph; a given-value gap, not introduced by this revision.
No gain or phase margin quantity is recorded on any node; computing one needs the same missing plant model.
No design case is stated and no margin values exist anywhere to check against a floor.

control.tilt_estimator.json (sensor-fusion estimator) is in the balance loop, so the trigger is present, but no margin of any kind is ever computed (D7/D8), so there is nothing to confirm was measured on the right loop; this is a given-value gap on balance_loop/tilt_estimator, untouched by this revision.
No lower gain margin (or s_m alternative) is recorded anywhere.
No M_s or M_T value is recorded anywhere.
No gain margin value exists on which to check units.
h*omega_c cannot be checked: no crossover frequency omega_c is stated or derivable for control.speed_loop or control.balance_loop from the data in the graph.
No continuous-time margin computation exists to check the hold/filter cost against.

The [B: p] bounds (p*tau_total<0.5, p*tau_common<2) cannot be evaluated (p missing, as D3/D6). The Cat.2 stating lines (tau_total, tau_common) are also absent for the balance loop, a given-value gap this revision did not touch.
No A/D resolution or coefficient word length is stated anywhere, and no code or coefficient implementation exists in the worktree to evaluate for quantisation sensitivity.

Magnitude limit is present (firmware.motor_output.json: motor_voltage_limit=6 V, max_duty_cycle=0.833). The rate limit is absent from every electrical/firmware node (electrical.motor_drivers.json gives only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage and thermal_resistance for the DRV8838 - no PWM frequency or slew-rate figure from which a rate limit could be derived); anti-windup is n/a since no integral action exists (per D18).

The [B: largest disturbance] and [B: a limit missing per D21] inputs are absent from the graph and not derivable (no disturbance magnitude is recorded anywhere, and D21's rate limit is missing); the base recovery-runs requirement is additionally undecidable because D1's region is undefined.

The [B: largest disturbance] input is absent from the graph and not derivable (no spec is issued and no disturbance magnitude is recorded); the 'no simulation includes the declared limit' aspect is a given-value gap (firmware.motor_output.json's limit is present but untouched by this revision, and no simulation exists at all).

design/journal.jsonl revs 30-35 show sample_rate changed 100→200 Hz consistently on every node that control.req_sample_rate constrains and every downstream constrains edge (D28 is satisfied numerically). But the change is unargued: control.req_sample_rate.json's source text is identical boilerplate before and after, with no ω_gc, no ratio h·ω_c or ω·h, and no plant model anywhere in design/nodes/*.json to ground it, violating D13 and S5, and leaving D6/D17/D29/D30's sample-rate-dependent stating lines undischarged. The revision is therefore not consistent with this rubric even though it is internally consistent in its own arithmetic.

No node states a tilt-angle, speed, or load validity range for any plant model; every node's 'model' field is null (e.g. design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json). This predates the revision and does not involve the sample_rate value the revision wrote, so it is a given-value gap, not charged to the revision.

No closed-loop pole computation appears anywhere in the design graph; no moment of inertia, centre-of-mass height, or other first-principles plant datum exists from which the state matrix or its eigenvalues could be derived (only mass=330 g and height=118.2 mm are given, insufficient to derive p).
No Nyquist encirclement count or pole computation exists anywhere; same missing plant-model gap as D3, unrelated to the written sample_rate value.
No S/PS/CS/T stability computation or root check of Kd·s²+Kp·s+Ki exists anywhere in the design graph (no Kd/Ki even declared, only a bare 'loop_gain').

control.balance_loop.json / control.req_sample_rate.json never state ω_gc, n_gc, τ_total, τ_common or a common RHP zero, even though τ_total/τ_common depend directly on h, which this revision changed from 0.01 s to 0.005 s (rev 30-32 in journal.jsonl). This stating line is 'owed regardless of [B]' and ties directly to the written sample_rate, so its absence is an ordinary finding, not missing evidence. (The bound itself additionally cannot be checked because p is missing - see spec_defects.)

No node lists the right-half-plane zeros of the fed-back tilt signal, not even a 'none found' statement, even though digital sampling can introduce sampling zeros dependent on h, and the revision changed h. This stating line is 'owed regardless of [B]' (none found would be 'met, not n/a') and was not discharged.

No sourced bandwidth is stated for the motor/driver or the IMU/filter anywhere in the design graph (electrical.motors.json and electrical.imu.json give voltage/current/speed data only, no bandwidth), and the sampling-limited bandwidth f_s/3 changed with this revision's sample-rate write without any accompanying statement or comparison to ω_gc.
